title: Roll Royale ( Ludo )
rules:
1. General Guidelines:
    • One participant per team.
    • Participants must report at least 10 minutes before their scheduled match.
    • Participants will be placed in groups of three or four through a draw of lots. No participant will receive a bye.
    • For Round 2, board and playing colour will be decided through a draw of lots.
    • The number of players qualifying from Rounds 1 and 2 will be announced before the event begins.
  2. Standard Ludo Rules (Rounds 2 and 3):
    • Each player will have four tokens of one colour.
    • At the start, one token will already be on the starting square. The other tokens can be brought out by rolling a 6.
    • Each player will roll the die once. The player with the highest number will start. If tied, roll again.
    • The game will continue clockwise.
    • Move a token according to the number rolled on the die.
    • Once a token is moved and released, the move cannot be changed.
    • If there is no valid move, the turn ends.
    • Rolling a 6 gives one extra turn.
    • Three consecutive 6s will end the turn, and the third roll will not be played.
    • Tokens on safe squares cannot be captured.
    • Landing on an opponent's token will send it back home, unless it is on a safe square.
    • Capturing an opponent's token gives one extra turn.
    • An exact number is needed to enter the home triangle.
    • The aim is to move all four tokens to the home triangle before the other players.
  3. Additional Rules:
    • An eliminated participant cannot re-enter the competition.
    • Help from teachers, audience members or other participants is not allowed.
    • The organisers' decision will be final in case of any dispute.
  4. Round 1 - Online Preliminary Round:
    • Participants will play online in groups of three or four decided through a draw of lots.
    • Participants must use their own mobile phone. Tablets and laptops are not allowed. Organisers will not provide mobile phones.
    • All players in a group must join the same online Ludo game/room given by the organisers.
    • Each match will have a time limit of 25 minutes. The number of players qualifying for Round 2 will be announced before the event begins.
    • If the match is not completed in 25 minutes, players will be ranked first by the number of tokens at home and then by which remaining tokens are closest to home.
    • If there is still a tie, 5 extra minutes will be given. If the tie remains, the tied players will roll a die and the highest number will qualify.
  5. Round 2 - Qualifying Round:
    • Players who qualify from Round 1 will compete in Round 2.
    • Players will be placed in groups of three or four through a draw of lots. Board and colour will also be decided by draw of lots.
    • Each match will have a time limit of 25 minutes.
    • The number of players qualifying for the Final Round will be announced before the event begins.
    • If the match is not completed in 25 minutes, the same ranking and tie-break rules used in Round 1 will apply.
  6. Round 3 - Final Round:
    • Players who qualify from Round 2 will compete in the Final Round.
    • Playing colours will be decided through a draw of lots.
    • The Final Round will have a time limit of 25 minutes.
    • The first player to bring all four tokens to the home triangle will be declared the winner.
    • If the match is not completed in 25 minutes, players will be ranked first by the number of tokens at home and then by which remaining tokens are closest to home.
    • If there is still a tie, 5 extra minutes will be given. If the tie remains, the tied players will roll the die and the highest number will win.
